description:
Name each engine-owned actor once as an `Assignee` constant.

## Background

System actors are string literals: `system:list` (`crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs:530`), `system:check` (`:578`), `system:admin` (`:630`), `system:recovery` (`:700`) and `system:lease-check` (`commands/mod.rs:729`). The automated gate executor is `AUTO_EXECUTOR: &str = "auto:executor"` (`gate_execution.rs:24`). `Assignee` (`domain/types.rs:281`) holds two private `String` fields, so it cannot be a `const`. `VirtualPath` shows the crate's way to build constants with `Cow<'static, str>` fields and a `const fn` (`repository_state/path.rs:249-254`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `Assignee` can be built in a const context, and its public API, parsing and serialized form are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: Associated `Assignee` constants name the list, check, admin, recovery and lease-check system actors and the automated gate executor.
- [hard] REQ-03: No production code spells a `system:` actor or `auto:executor` literal outside those constants.
- [hard] REQ-04: A unit test shows that each constant equals the result of parsing its spelling.
title: System actors are named Assignee constants
